steps.title: When headlights are a must
steps.body: Use headlights at night on unlit roads, and whenever visibility is seriously reduced.

options.text: Only on motorways
Only when other drivers switch theirs on
At night on an unlit road

question.explanation: Unlit roads at night and seriously reduced visibility both require headlights.

steps.title: In town at night
steps.body: In built-up areas at night, use dipped headlights.

question.prompt: Driving through a lit town centre at night, you should use…

options.text: Sidelights only
Full beam for the best view
Dipped headlights

question.explanation: Built-up areas at night call for dipped headlights — seen without dazzling.

steps.scene: On a dark road, an oncoming car's full beam dazzles you and the road ahead disappears.

options.text: Flash your own full beam back at them
Slow down, and stop if you need to
Keep your speed and look away from the light

question.explanation: If dazzled, slow down and if necessary stop — never retaliate with your own beam.

steps.title: Don't dazzle others
steps.body: Dip your headlights for oncoming traffic and when you're following another vehicle.

question.prompt: Following another car at night, you should…

options.text: Use full beam so they can see further too
Switch your lights off briefly
Dip your headlights

question.explanation: Full beam in a following position dazzles through their mirrors — dip it.

a.label: Visibility under 100 m
a.body: Fog lights allowed — visibility is seriously reduced.

b.label: Fog lifting
b.body: You must switch fog lights off as visibility improves.

question.prompt: Your rear fog lights are on and the fog clears. You must…

options.text: Switch them off
Keep them on in case fog returns
Leave them on until you park

question.explanation: Fog lights must go off when visibility improves — they dazzle and hide your brake lights.

steps.wrongBelief: Fog lights make you safer in any rain or drizzle.

options.text: Fog lights don't work in rain
They're only for seriously reduced visibility — generally under 100 m
It isn't wrong — brighter is always safer

question.explanation: Use fog lights only when visibility is seriously reduced, generally below 100 m.

steps.repairNote: Fog lights are for fog-level visibility, under about 100 m. In ordinary rain they just dazzle drivers behind.

questions.prompt: On an unlit road at night you must…

options.text: Use your headlights
Use hazard warning lights
Use sidelights only

questions.explanation: Headlights are required at night on unlit roads.

questions.prompt: In a built-up area at night, use…

options.text: Front fog lights
Dipped headlights
Full beam

questions.explanation: Dipped headlights keep you visible without dazzling in town.

questions.prompt: If you're dazzled by oncoming headlights, you should…

options.text: Speed up to pass them sooner
Flash your full beam in reply
Slow down and stop if necessary

questions.explanation: Slow down — and stop if you can't see. Retaliating blinds the other driver too.

questions.prompt: Visibility improves after fog. Your fog lights…

options.text: Can stay on for the rest of the trip
Must be switched off
Should be left on whenever it's cloudy

questions.explanation: You must switch fog lights off when visibility improves.

questions.prompt: Whatever the time of day, you must use headlights when…

options.text: Visibility is seriously reduced
The sky is overcast
You join any dual carriageway

questions.explanation: Seriously reduced visibility — generally under 100 m — means headlights on.
